messages.content: Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle

reasoning:
The user wants an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle. Let me make something charming and well-crafted. I'll build a nice SVG with a bicycle, a pelican with a big beak/pouch, maybe a scarf fluttering, motion lines, sun, ground.

Let me design carefully.

Canvas: 800x600.

Background: warm sky gradient, sun, ground strip.

Bicycle: two wheels with spokes, frame, handlebars, seat, pedals, chain.

Pelican: sitting on the seat, body, wing gripping handlebars, long beak with pouch, eye, legs pedaling, maybe a little helmet or scarf.

Let me set coordinates.

Wheels: radius 70, centers at (230, 430) and (560, 430). Ground line at y=500.

Frame: classic diamond frame. Points:
- Rear wheel hub: (230, 430)
- Front wheel hub: (560, 430)
- Bottom bracket (crank center): (375, 425)
- Seat tube top (seat): (350, 300)
- Head tube top (handlebars): (520, 290)
- Head tube bottom: (505, 330)

Frame tubes:
- Seat tube: (375,425) → (350,300)
- Down tube: (375,425) → (505,330)
- Top tube: (350,300) → (520,290)  hmm actually top tube goes from seat tube top to head tube top.
- Seat stay: (230,430) → (350,300)
- Chain stay: (230,430) → (375,425)
- Fork: (520,290) → (560,430) passing through head tube bottom.

Handlebars: from (520,290) going up to (525,270) then curve back to right/left. Let's make drop bars or upright bars. Upright cruiser bars curving back toward the pelican: from stem at (520, 285) up to (530, 262) then curve left to (480, 250) grip.

Actually pelican's wing reaches forward to grip handlebars around (505, 258).

Seat: at (350, 300) — seat shape ellipse-ish at (345, 292).

Pelican body: sits above the seat. Body center around (360, 230), an oval tilted. Neck goes up-forward to head around (500, 150). Beak long forward and downward pouch.

Legs: from body bottom (~ (355, 275)) down to pedal. Crank: bottom bracket at (375, 425), crank arm length 35. Pedal positions: pedal 1 at (375+35*cos, ...). Let's put one pedal forward-up: (400, 405) and other back-down: (350, 445). Legs go to pedals.

Wheels spokes: draw 8 spokes per wheel via lines.

Chain: two lines from rear cog (230,430 r=20) to front chainring (375,425 r=32) tangents approximated as lines from (375, 425-32) → (230, 430-20) and bottom similarly. Fine.

Motion: speed lines behind, small dust puffs.

Pelican details:
- Body: big ellipse-ish shape, white with gray shading. Let's use a path.
- Wing: folded wing on side, shaped path, with tip reaching toward handlebar as an arm? Pelicans riding bikes—wing tip grips handlebar. I'll draw a wing that extends forward with the tip curling around grip.
- Head: circle radius ~30 at (495, 150).
- Beak: upper mandible long from head forward right, ~110 length; lower mandible with big pouch sagging below. Pouch curves down.
- Eye: small circle with highlight. Also little tuft feather on head.
- Scarf: cyan scarf around neck trailing behind.
- Helmet? Maybe a small yellow helmet would be cute. But pelican crest + helmet could be funny. I'll add a helmet perched atop head with strap—actually a helmet over the head but beak sticking out. Let's do a small navy helmet with a vent. Hmm, might clutter. A scarf is enough plus maybe goggles. Let's do a helmet — safety-first pelican is charming. But beak pouch big; helmet sits on crown.

Let me keep it: head circle, small feather tuft, plus a helmet? I'll include a light helmet with a strap line.

Let me actually draw and refine shapes numerically.

Body path: pelican body as a plump oval tilted, with a tail at back-left. Use path:
M 300 210
C 285 250, 305 285, 355 285   (belly bottom)
C 400 285, 420 260, 415 230
C 410 200, 390 175, 350 172
C 320 168, 305 185, 300 210 Z

Hmm the body should connect to the neck going forward-right toward head at (500,150). Body front-top around (410, 200) → neck curve up to (470, 160).

Let's design body as one shape including neck:

Path:
M 290 230  (back)
C 285 200, 300 175, 330 170   upper back
C 360 165, 385 170, 400 165   toward neck base
C 425 155, 445 145, 462 138   neck to head base
... then head separate circle.

Simpler: draw body ellipse, neck as thick curved path (stroke with round cap, wide), head circle. That's easier and looks good.

Body: ellipse centered (355, 230), rx 75, ry 62, rotated -12deg. Plus tail triangle pointing back-left at (280, 240).

Neck: path stroke width 26, from (400, 200) curve to (470, 155): M 400 205 C 420 180, 440 160, 470 150 with stroke 24, color same as body white, stroke-linecap round.

Head: circle (485, 148) r 27.

Beak: upper mandible from head front (505, 145) extending to (620, 165) with slight downward tip. Pouch: big sac below, bulging.

Beak path:
Upper: M 505 136 C 545 130, 585 138, 620 158 C 600 158 ... hmm.

Let's define beak shape as single path including pouch:
Start at head front-top: (500, 132)
Curve to tip: C 545 122, 590 130, 632 152  → tip at (632, 152)
Then lower edge back: C 600 160, 580 165, 560 168... then pouch bulge down: pouch hangs below the lower mandible: from tip go down-left, pouch bottom around (545, 210), then back to head bottom (505, 175).

Path:
M 500 130
C 545 120, 592 132, 634 154     (upper mandible top edge)
L 628 162                       (tip)
C 600 168, 585 172, 572 178     (start of pouch under tip)
C 585 205, 565 232, 535 230     (pouch bulge bottom)
C 510 228, 498 205, 497 180     (pouch back to throat)
Z

Hmm pouch shape: pelican pouch hangs below lower mandible. Looks like a banana-shaped sac. Let me refine: tip at (634,156). Pouch: lower edge from tip sweeps back: control points create bulge down to y=235 at x=560, then back to throat at (498, 185). Good enough.

Also add line dividing upper/lower mandible: stroke path from (505, 150) to (630, 158).

Eye: circle at (492, 140) r 5, plus tiny highlight. Also a little brow.

Head crest tuft: small feather spike at (470,120) pointing back-up.

Wing: on body side, path shape like a folded wing, with a forward-reaching arm. Let's make wing: 
M 330 205 C 360 195, 395 205, 405 225 (top edge) then wing tip extends forward-down toward handlebar: from (405, 225) line to grip area (470, 250)? Handlebar grip position — let me set grips at (500, 262). Wing tip reaches (495, 258).

Wing path:
M 320 200
C 355 185, 400 195, 420 220
C 445 245, 470 252, 495 256   (wing reaching to handlebar)
C 475 262, 450 262, 430 255
C 390 250, 345 245, 320 235
Z
That forms a wing sweeping forward. Add feather lines inside.

Legs: pelican legs from body bottom at (370, 280) down to pedal. Webbed feet on pedals.
Leg 1 (far leg, darker): from (360,278) to pedal at (345, 445)? crank lower-rear pedal. Let's compute chainring center (375,425), radius crank 38. Pedal A (forward, up): angle 40° → (375+38*cos(-40?)...). Let's just place pedal A at (405, 400) (forward-up) and pedal B at (345, 450) (rear-down). Crank arms: line from (375,425) to (405,400) and opposite to (345,450).

Near leg goes to forward pedal A: path M 375 275 C 395 300, 405 330, 408 360 then foot at (405, 398). Knee bend forward. Pelican legs are short; but for a bicycle reach is fine — extend legs.

Far leg goes to pedal B (345,450): M 360 278 C 350 310, 345 360, 345 445.

Feet: webbed foot shapes at pedals: three-toe triangular web.

Handlebar grips: bar goes up from head tube top (520, 288) to (528, 262) then curves back to left ending grip at (492, 256) and other side grip toward viewer at (540, 250)? For a side view, one grip visible near, one far. Let's do cruiser-style swept-back bars: stem at (520,288) up to (530,265), then bar sweeps back (left) to (480, 255) with grip. Wing tip holds grip at ~(492,256). Good.

Frame color: coral/red. Wheels dark navy with cream tires? Let's pick palette:

- sky: #f6e6c8 → #fbe9d0? Let's do a nice palette: dusk teal sky with warm sun. Hmm.

Palette idea: 
Background sky gradient: #ffe9c2 (top) to #ffd39a bottom? Or teal sky #a8dadc. Let's do fresh daytime: sky gradient from #cfeef7 to #f7f2e4. Sun #ffd166. Ground road #3e4c59? Better: ground band #6b8f71 grass with a tan path.

Bicycle: coral #ff6b6b frame, dark charcoal wheels #2b3a42, cream tires? Let's do tires dark #223 with tan rims #ffd166 spokes.

Pelican: body white #ffffff with soft gray-blue shading #dbe4ea, beak pouch orange #f2a65b / #ffb703, beak upper #ffd166 warm, feet orange, eye #2b3a42.

Scarf: teal #2a9d8f fluttering.

Add title? No text needed. Maybe subtle.

Add motion lines behind: horizontal dashes at left.

Let me also add a little shadow ellipse under the bike.

Also maybe small birds in sky, clouds. Keep tasteful.

Let me write the SVG with defs gradients.

Structure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 800 560">
defs: sky gradient, pouch gradient, wheel gradients, ground.

Elements order:
1. background rect sky
2. sun + rays
3. clouds
4. distant hills
5. grass band + road path
6. speed lines / dust
7. shadow ellipse
8. bicycle far parts (far wheel? both wheels visible; far wheel drawn same layer), chain, frame, wheels, fork, seat, handlebar
9. pelican far leg (behind body)
10. pelican body + tail, neck, head, beak, wing, near leg, scarf
11. pedal cranks and pedals drawn appropriately: crank + pedal for near side over legs? The near pedal should be over the near foot? Typically the foot sits on the pedal, so pedal drawn under foot. Order: crank arms+pedals drawn before legs, then feet on top. Actually far leg behind bike? Let's order: rear wheel, front wheel, frame, chain, cranks+pedals, far leg+far foot, pelican body, near leg+near foot, wing, head.

Hmm the far leg should be behind the frame/cranks and the near leg in front. Fine: draw far leg before frame? Simplify: draw bike first, then far leg (slightly darker), then body (covers leg top), then near leg, then wing, then head/scarf. Far leg drawn over frame is slightly wrong but visually okay if darker. Better: draw far leg first, then bike, then body, then near leg. Body drawn after bike covers seat. Order:
- wheels, frame, chain, cranks/pedals
- far leg + far foot (drawn after pedals so foot appears over far pedal — wrong-ish but subtle; instead draw far pedal after far foot) — let's just do: crank arm far + far pedal drawn, far leg, far foot over far pedal. Then frame over far leg? Frame color crossing leg — realistic bikes: far leg behind frame. So draw far leg before frame. Sequence: wheels → chain → far leg+far foot+far crank/pedal → frame → seat → handlebar/fork → body → neck/head → near crank arm+near pedal → near leg+near foot → wing → scarf → head details.

But near crank arm must be over frame; fine, draw near crank after frame. Near pedal after near crank, then near leg then foot over pedal? Foot sits on pedal so pedal beneath foot: draw pedal then foot. But then pedal overlaps leg? Leg drawn after pedal is fine; foot drawn last covers pedal top.

Let me define coordinates concretely and write the code with a helper for spokes (just explicit lines, 10 spokes each). I'll use <g transform> for spokes: define spokes as lines from hub outward using rotate transforms in a group. That's neat:

<g transform="translate(230,430)"> then 12 lines each rotated: <line x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="-62" transform="rotate(0)"/> etc. I can use a group with multiple <line> elements rotated in 30° increments. That's 12 lines per wheel — verbose but fine. Alternatively use a path with many lines. I'll write them out via a single path string with M and L commands? Rotation math manual... easier: use <g stroke> with lines each with rotate transform. I'll write 12 lines per wheel using rotate values 0..330 step 30. Reuse with <use> and defs! Define <g id="wheel"> containing tire circle, rim circle, spokes, hub. Then use twice with transform translate. Great — reduces verbosity.

Wheel definition centered at origin: outer tire circle r=70 stroke #1f2d34 width 12; rim circle r=62 stroke #f2c14a width 5; spokes 12 lines length 60 stroke #7d9199 width 2; hub circle r=8 fill #2b3a42.

Use: <use href="#wheel" transform="translate(230,430)"/> and front at (560,430). Note href with xlink for compatibility — use href (SVG2) works in modern browsers. I'll include xlink:href too? Simpler: just duplicate groups to be safe. I'll use <use href="#wheel"> — supported widely. Add xmlns:xlink and xlink:href as fallback? Modern is fine; I'll just write the group twice to be bulletproof. Eh, use <use href="#wheel" xlink:href="#wheel"> with xmlns:xlink declared. That's safe.

Ground: grass band y from 500 to 560, with road? Bike wheels bottom at y=430+70+6=506. So ground line at ~506. Grass rect from 506 to 560, color #7fb069, plus a lighter dirt path strip. Add small grass tufts and stones.

Shadow ellipse at (395, 508) rx 180 ry 14 fill dark opacity .18.

Sun: circle at (660, 90) r 44 fill #ffd166 with soft glow circle r 60 opacity .25. Rays maybe not needed.

Clouds: two soft cloud shapes white opacity .8 at (130,110) and (430, 80).

Hills: path across mid background around y 430-480 in soft green #a3c58d behind bike. Since bike occupies lower area, hills behind should be subtle above ground line: hills top at ~450. But bike wheels go to 506, hills behind them look okay.

Speed lines: dashes on left of bike: lines at (100,300), (60,360) etc with rounded caps, color #ffffff opacity .7 or teal. Add small motion swirl.

Also add a few flying fish? Fun: pelican carrying fish? Nope, keep focus.

Maybe the pelican has a small backpack or a mailbag? Keep it simple.

Let me now write coordinates for frame precisely:

rear hub R = (230, 430)
front hub F = (560, 430)
bottom bracket B = (378, 424)
seat cluster S = (352, 306)
head tube top HT = (512, 292)
head tube bottom HB = (500, 336)

Tubes (stroke #ff6b6b width 9, linecap round):
- seat tube: B→S
- top tube: S→HT
- down tube: B→HB
- head tube: HB→HT (stroke width 12 maybe darker)
- seat stays: R→S
- chain stays: R→B
- fork: HB→F (stroke width 8) — with slight curve? Straight line ok, cruiser fork straight.
- seat post: S→(348, 292) small; seat at (342, 288).

Handlebar: stem from HT (512,292) up: path M 512 292 L 522 268 then bar sweep: C 522 258, 512 250, 495 250 then grip to 480 252. Draw stroke #2b3a42 width 7, then grip ellipse/round cap thicker #ffd166? Let's make grips coral-dark or teal: stroke separate path width 12 linecap round color #2a9d8f from (497,249) to (483,253).

Wait: the swept-back bar goes backward (to the left). Wing grips around x 490. Good.

Also a front brake lever? skip.

Seat: path shape: M 322 292 C 330 282, 358 280, 372 288 C 372 296, 350 300, 330 298 Z fill #2b3a42. Seat post line from (352, 306) to (348, 296).

Hmm seat top around y=282-292; pelican body bottom around y=285. Body sits on seat — body bottom y ~ 285, so body overlaps seat. Fine: draw seat before body; body covers most of seat, rear part visible.

Chainring at B: circle r 26 fill none stroke #f2c14a width 3 with dashed? Use circle with stroke-dasharray for teeth: stroke-dasharray "4 4" width 6 color #ffd166. Chain: lines from chainring top tangent to rear cog top: chainring r=26 at (378,424), rear cog r=16 at (230,430). Chain path: M 378 398 L 230 414 (top) and M 378 450 L 230 446 (bottom) plus arcs around cog. Draw as a single path: M 230 414 L 378 398 A 26 26 0 0 1 378 450 L 230 446 A 16 16 0 0 1 230 414 Z stroke #6b7b85 width 5 fill none. Direction of arcs: from (378,398) around right side to (378,450): sweep flag 1 with r 26 → goes clockwise to the right. Yes good. Rear cog arc from (230,446) to (230,414) sweep 1 goes... left side? With sweep=1 (clockwise) from bottom point to top point, clockwise passes through left side (x < 230). Actually clockwise from (230,446) going... Let's check: clockwise direction in SVG coordinates (y down) means going from bottom point to top point the arc bulges to the left? Consider circle center (230,430). Point (230,446) is bottom (angle 90° in math-y-down terms). Going clockwise (in screen terms, visually clockwise): bottom → left → top. Yes visually clockwise from bottom goes to the left side. Correct, sweep=1 gives left bulge. Good.

Crank arms: near crank from B (378,424) to pedal near Pn = (412, 402)? crank length 40: direction forward-up. Let's compute: angle forward-up = direction (0.7,-0.55) normalized ~ (0.73,-0.6)*40 = (29,-24) → Pn=(407, 400). Far pedal Pf = opposite = (349, 448).

Draw far crank first: line B→Pf stroke #6b7b85 width 7, pedal rect at Pf rotated: small rounded rect 26x8 fill #2b3a42. Near crank: line B→Pn stroke #cbd5db width 7, pedal at Pn.

Foot positions: near foot on Pn (407,400), far foot on Pf (349,448).

Legs: pelican legs short-ish. Near leg: hip at (365, 275). Path: M 365 272 C 392 285, 400 320, 396 355 C 394 380, 402 394, 407 400 → foot. Draw stroke #f2a65b? M 0 0 L 22 6 L 14 10 L 20 16 L 8 14 L 12 20 L 0 12 Z? Hmm webbed foot: draw triangle with scalloped front: path "M -8 -4 L 18 4 C 20 6 20 8 18 10 L 12 12 L 16 18 L 6 16 L 10 22 L 2 18 Z" too fiddly.

Simpler: foot = rounded triangle web: 
path d="M 0 -6 L 20 2 Q 24 6 18 9 L 6 14 Z" plus toe lines. I'll do:
<g transform="translate(407,398)"> <path d="M -10 -6 L 20 0 C 26 2 26 10 20 12 L -2 14 C -10 12 -14 4 -10 -6 Z" fill="#f2a65b"/> toe separation lines stroke. </g>
That's a blobby webbed foot over the pedal. Add 2 thin lines to suggest toes: M 6 0 L 12 12, M 0 -4 L 8 14.

Let's do: yellow helmet #ffd166 with vents, sits atop head; tufts peek out behind. Strap: thin line from helmet down front behind beak. I think this adds personality. Let's do it: helmet as arc path over head circle center (486,146) r 28: helmet covers top: path M 458 142 A 28 28 0 0 1 514 140 L 512 138? Let's make helmet shape: 
path d="M 456 145 A 30 30 0 0 1 516 141 C 516 148 512 152 504 150 L 466 152 C 458 152 455 150 456 145 Z" fill #ffd166 stroke #e0a92e width 2. M 502 130

L 630 158

L 505 150

C 528 226, 512 206, 508 180

Combine: draw pouch (with gradient) first, then upper mandible on top. Add a line along lower mandible edge stroke #d97b3a.

Careful: pouch extends below head into neck area; neck goes from body (400,200) to head (470,150). Pouch bottom around (556,222) floats in front — fine visually.

Also the pouch overlapping the scarf? Scarf at neck around x 450, y 170 — pouch back edge x 508 → scarf knot at 452 fine, scarf behind pouch (draw scarf before head/pouch? scarf knot in front of neck but behind pouch). Order: body → neck → scarf → pouch/head → beak → helmet → wing? Wing reaches handlebar low (y 250) not conflicting.

Order plan:
bg → sun → clouds → hills → grass → speed lines → shadow → wheels → chain → far crank/pedal → far leg+foot → frame tubes → head tube/fork → seat → handlebar → chainring → tail → body → neck → scarf knot+tails → pouch+lower beak → head circle → upper mandible → eye/brow/nostril → helmet → tufts → near crank+pedal → near leg+foot → wing.

Wait: near leg drawn after body good. Wing drawn after legs? Wing is on the near side, above body; wing should be over body and its tip over handlebar grip. Draw wing after handlebar. But near leg drawn after handlebar? no conflict.

Also chainring drawn after frame; near crank drawn after chainring.

Let me also add small "ding" bell on handlebar: little circle #ffd166 at (530, 258) with dome — cute. Add bell near grip: circle r 6 fill #f2c14a at (528,256)? Handlebar stem there. Grass below and above? Let's do: grass band 506→560 fill green; a light tan track ellipse-ish band: rect 0-800, y 500-520 fill #dfc9a0 opacity .9, then wheels sit on tan band top y=500? Wheels bottom at y=430+70(tire center r)+6 stroke half = 506. So surface line at 506. Set tan band y 504→524. Grass from 504 down? Hmm overlapping: Draw grass rect y 504→560 (#7fb069 top with gradient), then tan track path y 506→526 drawn over grass, then small grass tufts along top of grass line outside track. Wheels bottom touch y=506, sitting on tan track. Good. Shadow ellipse at y 506.

Also add distant trees? Two simple round trees behind: circles cluster #6f9e62 at x 80 y 460 and x 720 y 445 with trunk. Keep subtle. Front wheel is at x 560, sun at 660,90. Trees at (700, 470) ok behind bike.

Small birds silhouette in sky: two "V" strokes at (200, 120). ok.

Let's write final SVG carefully with valid syntax.

Spokes: I'll define group with 12 lines:
<g id="wheel">
 <circle r="70" fill="none" stroke="#22343c" stroke-width="12"/>
 <circle r="62" fill="none" stroke="#f2c14a" stroke-width="5"/>
 <g stroke="#8fa3ab" stroke-width="2.5">
  <line y2="-58" />
  <line y2="-58" transform="rotate(30)"/> ... etc
 </g>
 <circle r="9" fill="#3a4c56"/>
 <circle r="4" fill="#f2c14a"/>
</g>
Note lines need x1=0 x2=0 defaults 0. OK.

Then <use href="#wheel" x="230" y="430"/> — `use` with x,y attributes translates. That works! x/y on use translate. Great: <use href="#wheel" x="230" y="430"/>.

But defs element inside <defs>, use references. Add xlink namespace & xlink:href for older renderers: I'll add xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" and xlink:href="#wheel" alongside href.

Now write everything.

Frame tube group: stroke="#ff6b6b" stroke-width="9" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none". Lines:
seat tube: M378 424 L352 306
top tube: M352 306 L512 292
